column1: # Bench panel: Ahmed et al. 2020 (doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0241584), lipL32 real-time
# PCR for pathogenic Leptospira. Read 2026-10-26 from papers/10.1371_journal.pone.0241584.pdf
# Table 1, which scores 73 strains as + or - across pathogenic, intermediate and
# saprophytic species. All 60 pathogenic strains are +, all 13 intermediate and
# saprophytic strains are -.
# WHAT THIS PANEL IS A TEST OF. A hydrolysis-probe assay whose published positives
# the current scoring rule calls `fail`, every one of them on a single mismatch at
# position 1 from the reverse primer's 3' terminus, which `terminal_mismatch_fails`
# treats as fatal on its own. Paired with a calicivirus Hel1 panel on a conventional
# PCR, it gives that one knob a TWO-CHEMISTRY test, which is the point: the rule is
# a qPCR-strength rule applied to 155 conventional entries and 51 probe ones.
# THREE SUBSTITUTIONS, because Table 1 prints no accessions. Each is a real
# departure from what the paper did and none is hidden:
# 1. The label is the paper's SPECIES-level verdict; the paper tested STRAINS. Every
#    pathogenic strain scored +, so a species-level reading is faithful for the
#    positives. L. meyeri is the exception and is EXCLUDED: Table 1 scores it BOTH
#    ways, + for serovar Sofia (row 42, pathogenic) and - for serovar Semaranga
#    (row 69, saprophytic), so no species-level label is honest for it.
# 2. The accession is a representative GenBank record of that species, not the
#    strain the paper tested, which is the same substitution the Forslund and Rahn
#    panels make (a reference genome per type or serovar).
# 3. Where a species' records do not agree, the representative is the MODAL call's
#    record, preferring a complete genome. The distribution is printed below so the
#    choice cannot hide a split. Picked against results/2026-10-25/calls.tsv.gz.
# Per-species call distribution on that run, so the representative is auditable:
#   adleri fail:4 | alexanderi reduced:5 detect:2 | alstonii detect:5
#   barantonii fail:2 detect:1 | borgpetersenii detect:359 no_amplicon:74 fail:10 reduced:5
#   broomii fail:1 | ellisii fail:2 | fainei fail:1 | gomenensis fail:8
#   inadai fail:3 | interrogans detect:998 no_amplicon:203 reduced:1
#   kirschneri detect:93 no_amplicon:1 | kmetyi fail:14 | licerasiae no_amplicon:7
#   mayottensis reduced:28 | noguchii detect:46 no_amplicon:1
#   santarosai detect:54 reduced:35 no_amplicon:19 | weilii detect:30 reduced:1 no_amplicon:1
#   wolffii fail:15
# EIGHT TABLE 1 SPECIES ARE NOT ROWS, because the retrieval archive holds no usable
# nuccore record for them: dzianensis and putramalaysiae (+), biflexa, idonii,
# terpstrae, vanthielii, wolbachii and yanagawae (-). L. biflexa is present only as
# an assembly accession, which efetch -db nuccore cannot fetch. So the panel is 19
# of the 27 species Table 1 names, 14 band and 5 no_band.
# TWO LIMITS ON WHAT IT CAN BE USED FOR, both from the test plan:
# - It is this assay's OWN design and validation paper, so it cannot enter
#   docs/validation-cases.tsv, which excludes an assay's own panel. One assay and
#   one paper also means its rows are correlated, not independent evidence.
# - Its informative rows are false NEGATIVES of the scoring rule, so they do NOT
#   count toward the 40 within-family negatives that gate the Bayesian C2 model.
